ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a series circuit, with an AC voltage source on the left, labeled sin(ωt); there is a switch at the top, with a label beside it indicating that it operates at t=t0; to the right of the switch, a 5 Ω resistor and a 0.01 H inductor are connected in series in sequence, finally returning to the source to form a loop. Reasoning: Before the switch is closed, the branch is open, so the current is 0; the inductor current is continuous, so i(t0+)=i(t0-)=0. If there is no transient component after closing, then the actual current at the instant of closing must be equal to the current value of this RL series circuit in sinusoidal steady state. For the voltage source sin(ωt), the RL series steady-state current can be written as i_ss(t)=Im sin(ωt-φ), where φ=tan^(-1)(ωL/R). To make the transient term zero, i_ss(t0)=0 is required, so ωt0-φ=0 mod π. Taking the smallest positive value: t0=φ/ω. Given f=50 Hz, ω=2πf=100π rad/s. Thus φ=tan^(-1)((ωL)/R)=tan^(-1)((100π×0.01)/5)=tan^(-1)(0.6283)≈0.561 rad. Therefore t0=0.561/(100π) s≈0.00178 s=1.78 ms.

raw_record.question_text: Consider the circuit shown in the figure. If the frequency of the source is 50 Hz, then a value of \( t_0 \) which results in a transient free response is _____ ms.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a source sin(ωt), a switch closing at t=t0, and a series R=5 Ω, L=0.01 H branch. Use the text frequency f=50 Hz to set ω=2πf. Since the branch is open before t0, impose i(t0+)=i(t0-)=0. Write the steady-state current for the series RL as i_ss(t)=I_m sin(ωt-φ), where φ=tan^{-1}(ωL/R). The full switched response has a transient term proportional to [i(t0)-i_ss(t0)]e^{-R(t-t0)/L}; eliminate it by setting i_ss(t0)=0. Hence choose ωt0-φ=0 mod π; the smallest positive value is t0=φ/ω. Substitute R=5, L=0.01, f=50 to get t0≈1.78 ms.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a sine source is connected through a timed switch to a 5 Ω resistor in series with a 0.01 H inductor. From the text, f=50 Hz, so ω=2π·50. Compute the load impedance Z=R+jωL=5+j(ω·0.01), whose phase angle is θ=tan^{-1}(ωL/R). The steady-state current lags the source voltage by θ, so its zero crossings occur θ/ω seconds after the source-voltage zero crossings, plus half-period repeats. Because the initial current in the open inductor is 0, choose one of those zero-current instants for switch closure; the first positive one is t0=θ/ω. Numerically this gives t0≈tan^{-1}(0.6283)/314.16≈1.78 ms.
